messages.subject: data input for sim.cross 4way
parts:
Hello,

I'm trying to use the sim.cross function to run some QTL mapping
simulations, but I'm struggling to generate simulated 4way cross data.
The problem I'm having is with inputing the QTL locations and effects
for the female and male maps separately. I'm probably missing something
obvious, but I can't find an example anywhere in the help files.
Anyway, here is what I've tried so far:

fakemap<-sim.map(len=rep(100,20), n.mar=15, include.x=F, sex.sp=T) #to
make a fake map with no X chromosome

fakecross<-sim.cross(fakemap, type="4way", n.ind=98,
model=rbind(c(2,36,5,2,2), c(15,2,2,1,0))) #for 2 QTL

when I try to run the sim.cross, I get the following error message:
Error: invalid to set the class to matrix unless the dimension
attribute is of length 2 (was 0)

I'm really not sure why this is happening (when I examing the model
matrix outside the function it has the right length of dim attributes).
I would also appreciate any advice on simulating more than one
phenotypic trait at a time which is what's given in the fake.4way data
set.

Thanks in advance,

Arianne

messages.author: ab8dbe3bec292afe
messages.subject: Re: data input for sim.cross 4way
parts:
There is a bug in the simulation code for 4-way crosses. It is fixed
in the version that I intend to release in the next two weeks. The
source
code for my development version of the package is available at the
R/qtl web site:

http://www.rqtl.org/download

If you need a binary, I hope you can wait a couple of weeks.

karl
